MixSIARPFN: MixSIAR models fitted by prior-data fitted networks

Source: R/MixSIARPFN-package.R
MixSIARPFN-package.Rd

Load data with load_mix_data(), load_source_data() and load_discr_data() as in MixSIAR, fit with run_pfn() (in place of write_JAGS_model() and run_model()), and summarise with output_pfn() (in place of output_JAGS()). The posteriors come from networks trained on simulations from MixSIAR's model, one per error structure, downloaded on first use (see pfn_networks()).

Details

The example data are from MixSIAR (Stock et al. 2018, PeerJ 6:e5096): the killer whale, geese and wolves vignettes.

Limitations

  • Marginal posteriors only. Each proportion and parameter has its own posterior, but there are no joint draws: the marginal means of one diet need not sum to exactly 1, and sums, differences or ratios of proportions cannot be computed.

  • Accuracy. On data simulated from MixSIAR's model the 95% intervals are calibrated but 5 to 12% wider than MixSIAR's, and the posteriors a little less accurate (CRPS 2 to 5% higher than fully converged MixSIAR; see vignette("performance")).

  • Weakly identified sources. Where the data cannot pin a source down, the network tends to put more probability near 0 than MixSIAR does.

  • No model checks. Without joint draws, posterior predictive checks cannot be run; where it matters, check the model with a MixSIAR run. The geese and wolves vignettes show MixSIAR's model failing such a check, and the two fits differing most where it fails.

  • Envelope. Up to 8 sources, 4 tracers, two categorical effects and one continuous effect, with source summary statistics only; data outside what the networks were trained for are refused.
